messages:
olivia: Customer (acme-inc) reports 422 from POST /v1/rerank. They include both top-level query and a nested "query" field inside a document object. Can someone confirm if this is by-design?

olivia: repro below (redacted token):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"how to reset password","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"reset steps..."}],"documents":[{"id":"d-42","title":"internal-note","query":"admin-intent"}]}'
```

olivia: Response they get: 422 Unprocessable Entity
```json
{ "error": "Ambiguous field \"query\" - collisions between request root and document object" }
```

ian: :thinking: I can repro this locally. If root has "query" and a document has the same key at the top level of the doc object our validator treats it as ambiguous and returns 422.

zoe: This is an input-shape problem, yes. Our API spec reserves a few top-level names (query, collection, limit). Nested metadata is allowed but we intentionally validate against collisions at any level to avoid accidental shadowing.

olivia: Customer insists they used "query" inside doc metadata for their own scoring signals. They can't rename easily (third-party pipeline). Any short-term workaround?

ryan: Short term: tell them to move nested flags under a "metadata" object or rename "query" -> "doc_query". Example that works:
```json
{"query":"how to reset password","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"reset steps..."}],"documents":[{"id":"d-42","title":"internal-note","metadata":{"query":"admin-intent"}}]}
```

zoe: We should also improve the error message to point to the path and suggest renaming. Current 422 is cryptic. I'll open a PR to include the conflicting JSON Pointer in the response (e.g., /documents/0/query) and a suggestion.

ian: For long-term: we can either allow namespacing for document-level keys (preferable) or add an explicit list of reserved keys that are only reserved at root-level. Changing validator behavior might risk breaking customers who relied on current strictness. Needs eng-ml signoff.

olivia: Customer also reported a billing alert triggered by repeated 422s (rate of failures made them hit error billing thresholds). They want a temporary opt-out so we don't count failed calls toward their meter. Is that possible?

ryan: Billing team: we can ignore 4xx failures for invoiceable token counts, but it's a policy change and needs approvals. Short-term we can issue a credit for the window if they provide timestamps.

zoe: Action items: 1) Devex/Docs - add note in rerank docs about reserved top-level keys and example namespace pattern. 2) Eng-ML - evaluate relaxing validator vs namespacing policy. 3) Billing - consider credit for customer if they provide logs. 4) CS - provide customer workaround and repro steps.

ian: I attached stacktrace snippet from local run (abbreviated):
```
ValidationError: FieldCollision(query) at /documents/0/query
    at validateRequest (/opt/redwood/api/validators.js:412)
    at rerankHandler (/opt/redwood/api/rerank.js:88)
```

olivia: Sent workaround to customer (use metadata or rename). They confirmed rename works. They've requested we escalate to eng-ml for a better developer UX.

ops-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-0938 — rerank input-collision. Assigned to eng-ml.

zoe: I'll follow up with a minimal spec change proposal and a docs patch today. If eng-ml wants to relax validation we'll schedule a careful rollout with a feature flag.

olivia: Thanks all — I'll mark this high priority for the customer and keep the thread updated. :white_check_mark:
